title: Give an epinephrine auto-injector trainer into a training pad, release straight off, click, hold 3 s, back on the tray
instruction: Give the trainer auto-injector into the target on the training pad: pull off the blue safety release, press the orange tip into the pad until it clicks, hold it there for 3 seconds, then lay the trainer back on the tray.
context: Registered nurses (BLS 29-1141, about 3.3 million US jobs) have the task 'Administer medications to patients and monitor patients for reactions or side effects' (O*NET 29-1141.00). An epinephrine auto-injector, used on the outer thigh, is the emergency treatment for anaphylaxis (food allergy: 10.8% of US adults, Gupta 2019). The maker's steps for the real pen, taught on the needle-free trainer in every EpiPen 2-Pak: orange tip down, blue release pulled straight off, tip pressed firmly against the outer thigh at a right angle until it clicks, held 3 seconds (Viatris leaflet). Published force: 23 N to fire an EpiPen Jr (Schwirtz & Seeger, J Asthma Allergy 2010); every 0.3 mg EpiPen activation under 50 N (2012). The skill is in standing a pen that lies on a tray tip down in one hand, taking the release off with the other, then pressing square on a curved target and keeping it pushed in for 3 s, here with the needle-free trainer on a training pad.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. Injection pad: a Limbs & Things 00310 Injection Trainer (21 x 16 x 11 cm, 0.6 kg; skin, fat and muscle layers), lying on the table with its long side along y, center at (30.0, -9.0); a 6 x 4 cm target outline is drawn on its cover at the top of its crown (6 cm along the pad, 4 cm across the crown). Tray: a white plastic medication tray 22 x 14 cm, center at (24.0, -27.5), with a white foam rest 16 x 5 x 1 cm on it whose 2.4 cm groove runs along x. Pen: an EpiPen Trainer (Viatris, gray, labeled TRAINER; 14 cm with its release, 2.1 cm across; needle-free and drug-free; it ships loose in the carton, without a carrier tube) lying in the groove, blue safety release on, orange tip toward the robot. Room 20-24 C. Both arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: The pen fires when its orange sleeve is pushed 7 mm into the body (the click; 23 N in the simulation), which the sleeve cannot do while the blue release is on its pin. It fires on target when the tip is on the pad's cover inside the 6 x 4 cm target and the pen is within 20 degrees of the skin's normal there, orange end into the pad. It is held when, for 3 s after the click, the sleeve stays pushed in at least 4 mm with the tip on the target and square. The trial scores 1.0 when the pen fired on target, was held 3 s, and lies on the tray (its middle inside the tray's outline, within 3 cm above it, its axis within 30 degrees of level), let go by both hands and still for 1 s. It scores 0.75 when fired on target and held 3 s but not yet laid down, let go or still; 0.5 when fired on target but lifted, let off or slid off the target before 3 s; 0.25 when the release is off and the pen has not fired. Any other end state scores 0; doing nothing scores 0. The whole trial scores 0 if the pen fires anywhere but the target (into the air, the table, beside the target, at a slant or blue end first) or falls off the table. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Real trial (outcome only): the trainer's click (audible on video), the tip's mark inside the target outline (photo), the angle to the pad surface's normal against printed 20-degree cards (the crown's profile along the pad, a plain card across it) and the hold counted in video frames (30 fps) from the click to the tip leaving the cover, then the pen photographed on the tray with both hands off and still for 1 s (README, Real-trial check).
reset_notes: Reset the trainer as its instructions say: replace the blue safety cap, place the orange tip on a hard surface, squeeze the sides of the orange tip and push down. Lay it in the groove at its tape mark, orange tip toward the robot; check the pad sits on its tape outline; wipe the tip's ink mark off the cover. About 30 s. In simulation the layout is identical every trial.
fidelity: Rigid pen with a sprung orange sleeve: 23 N at its 7 mm click (published EpiPen Jr force; the trainer's is unpublished), blocked while the release is on. The release is a loose cap over a 10 mm pin; its press fit is not modeled. The pad is rigid with its real size and crown; the tip within 4 mm of it is on the soft cover. Click and hold are read from the sleeve's position, not a force.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (1,200 steps); demo: 1.0 (781 steps). Both on task.py f5b0ce7947db.
